intro.heading: Roofing Built for Houston's Climate
intro.body_p1: No major U.S. city puts more cumulative stress on residential roofs than Houston. The area averages roughly 50 inches of rainfall per year — surpassing most coastal cities — and sits directly in the path of Atlantic hurricane and tropical storm systems that can deliver sustained winds well above design thresholds for standard asphalt shingles. Between hurricane seasons, the combination of intense UV exposure, high humidity, and extreme summer heat degrades shingles, flashing sealants, and underlayment faster than in drier climates. A Houston roof that is 15 years old has aged harder than a 15-year-old roof almost anywhere else in the country.
intro.body_p2: Home Team serves homeowners across the Greater Houston area with the same approach: a thorough, no-pressure inspection that documents what your roof actually looks like right now, followed by honest options and clear pricing. We work from our base in Tomball, making us well-positioned to serve northwest Houston, Harris County, and the surrounding communities. Whether you are assessing hurricane damage, dealing with a persistent leak, or planning ahead for a roof that is approaching the end of its useful life, we provide the information you need to make a confident decision.

items.q: How does Houston's hurricane exposure affect residential roofing?
items.a: Houston sits in one of the most hurricane-active coastal corridors in the United States. Even storms that make landfall south of the city can deliver sustained winds of 50–80 mph and higher gusts to the Houston metro area. Standard three-tab asphalt shingles are typically rated for winds up to 60–70 mph; architectural shingles with enhanced wind resistance can be rated considerably higher. After any named storm or significant wind event, a professional inspection is warranted — shingles can sustain structural damage that is not visible from the ground but significantly shortens the roof's remaining lifespan. Home Team offers free post-storm inspections throughout Greater Houston.

items.q: Houston gets around 50 inches of rain a year — what does that mean for my roof?
items.a: Fifty inches of annual rainfall means every potential vulnerability in your roofing system gets tested repeatedly. Flashing seals at chimneys, vents, skylights, and any roof penetration are exposed to driving rain multiple times per year, and any gap in a sealant allows water to enter slowly but consistently. Gutters and downspouts sized for drier climates may be unable to handle peak Houston rainfall rates, causing water to back up against the fascia. Underlayment condition matters more here than in drier cities because it is regularly called on to prevent the water that shingles alone cannot stop. Home Team evaluates drainage capacity and waterproofing details as part of every Houston-area inspection.

items.q: My Houston home has an older flat or low-slope section — does Home Team service those?
items.a: Houston's architectural diversity includes a significant number of homes with flat or low-slope roof sections — particularly on covered patios, garage extensions, and mid-century homes. These sections require different materials and installation techniques than pitched asphalt shingle roofing. Contact Home Team to discuss your specific situation; our team can assess the condition of low-slope areas and provide options appropriate for those roof types.

items.q: When is the right time to replace a roof in Houston versus repair it?
items.a: In Houston's climate, the calculus between repair and replacement tips toward replacement earlier than in milder areas. A roof approaching 15–20 years old on standard asphalt shingles has been through multiple hurricane seasons, tens of thousands of UV hours, and significant cumulative rainfall. If a roof in this age range shows widespread granule loss, multiple areas of damage, or has required repeated repairs, replacement usually delivers better long-term value than continued patch work. Home Team provides an honest assessment rather than defaulting to either option — we show you the actual condition and let you decide with full information.

topic1.heading: Intense Heat and UV Exposure
topic1.body: Houston-area summers push roof surface temperatures well above the ambient air temperature. Over time, heat and UV radiation break down shingle granules, accelerate asphalt oxidation, and shorten the functional life of an improperly ventilated roof. Quality attic ventilation is not optional in this climate — it is a performance requirement.

topic2.heading: Hurricane and Storm Exposure
topic2.body: Greater Houston sits in one of the most hurricane-active corridors in the United States. Even storms that make landfall away from the city can deliver sustained winds that stress or damage shingles, flashing, and ridge caps. Between hurricane seasons, frequent severe thunderstorms produce localized hail and high-wind events that can cause damage not visible from the ground.

topic3.heading: High Annual Rainfall
topic3.body: Houston averages among the highest annual rainfall of any major U.S. city. Frequent heavy rain events put every flashing seal, penetration, and drainage system on a residential roof under repeated stress. Gutters and downspouts sized for drier climates may be insufficient for peak Houston rainfall rates. Home Team evaluates drainage capacity and waterproofing details as part of every Houston-area inspection.

topic4.heading: Harris County Permits
topic4.body: Residential roof replacements in Harris County — including unincorporated areas of Greater Houston — require a county building permit. Work within incorporated city limits may require a separate city permit. Home Team confirms the applicable jurisdiction and permit requirements for your specific address and manages the permit process so you don't have to.
